note: Wire schema version 1 implies this dialect. A port that answers differently on any case below is not speaking version 1, whatever its expressions serialise to.

case_folding.why: full folding, not simple: one character folds to two
the same, against an already-lowercase subject
compatibility ligature folds to its letters
Kelvin sign folds to the ordinary letter
Greek final sigma and medial sigma fold together
no normalization: composed and decomposed are different text
no normalization: the dotted capital I keeps its combining dot

regex_grammar.why: backreferences are not in this grammar
lookbehind is not in this grammar
so is the Unicode word class

regex_ignore_case.why: a case-insensitive regex does NOT fold one character to two, which is where it parts company with the text operators above
regex_ignore_case.subject: Straße

regex_ignore_case.why: and not in the other direction either
regex_ignore_case.subject: STRASSE

regex_ignore_case.why: it does apply simple case folding, including the long s
regex_ignore_case.subject: ſ

regex_ignore_case.why: the ordinary case, so the flag is doing something
regex_ignore_case.subject: STRAAE
